findings.what: THE ACCEPTANCE NOBODY HAD TAKEN IS NOW TAKEN — a phone fought. arena_duel behind the real title, reference phone 844x390, every input a real CDP touch, no keyboard in the leg and no harness touch verb. Sentry 412 -> 311.2 hp; player 620 -> 436.28 (it hit back). Moves r1.1/r1.2 out of a finger; stamina 120 -> 98; roll i-frames invuln on 36/67 samples; a held finger gives guardRaised on 20/25 with state BLOCK_HOLD; and the strafing attack (stick + button, two fingers) travelled 0.997 m AND swung.

T6 measured on touch for the first time — the round named it unmeasured and correctly located the threshold in combat/player.js _chargeTick. A 60 ms hold on 'heavy' gives ['r1.1']; a 700 ms hold gives ['r2','r2.charged']. The charged variant appears only on the long hold, thresholded on duration exactly as T6 asks.

THE ROLL IS UNRELIABLE WHILE THE MOVEMENT STICK IS HELD. Four arms, one page, one body: a finger on the arc with no stick backsteps 5/5 (correct — a dodge with no direction is a backstep); a finger on the arc WITH a finger on the stick produced no move at all on 4/5 presses and a sprint on the fifth; the keyboard Space key with the SAME finger on the SAME stick rolls cleanly, as does the pure desktop arm. Rolling out of a run is the most-used verb in a Souls fight.
findings.not_confirmed_because: At the 9.9-11.6 fixed steps/s this build reaches at the phone profile on this box, a wall-clock tap is coarse, and I could not separate 'the touch button drops the tap when a second pointer is live' from 'at 12 Hz the tap lands between the frames that would have seen it'. What IS established is the ASYMMETRY: same box, same load, same body, same frame rate, and the desktop key rolls where the touch control does not. That cannot be explained by frame rate alone because both arms pay it.

findings.what: T5's GATE IS COUNTED IN FRAMES AND PRESSED IN MILLISECONDS. hold-gate.js is 12 fixed sim frames and the round proved the pad and the touchscreen share one implementation of it — all correct, and reproduced. But `--leg gate` drives the sim with stepFrames, where wall-clock time does not exist, so the harness cannot express this question. Measured in play mode with the press timed BY THE GAME (TouchInput stamps gateFrom on the down, sim.frame is read on the up): at 11.6 fixed steps/s, 12 frames is 1034 ms of thumb time; at a true 60 Hz it is 200 ms. The wall-clock cost of the roll/sprint discriminator is a function of frame rate, so RI-JRN04 T5's promise that pad semantics 'transfer' holds in frames and not in the hand.
findings.owed: an S-ruling, not a silence. An ms-based gate breaks determinism; a frame-based gate drifts with frame rate. Not the critic's call to make.

findings.what: NOBODY HAS MEASURED THE FRAME RATE, AND IT IS 10-12 Hz UNDER LOAD. 28.3 fixed steps/s at ~2.6 load/core, 9.9 at ~4.3, 11.6 at ~4.9, all at 844x390. The round said plainly that RI-PLT01/02 frame budgets were untouched, which is honest.
findings.must_be_read_with: These are headless SwiftShader on a contended shared box and they are NOT a phone's numbers. They are not evidence that a real device is slow. What they establish is that F4's coupling is real and load-sensitive, and that nobody has taken this measurement anywhere — so 'a phone can play a Souls-shaped fight' is established for the VERBS and not for the TIMING, and a Souls fight is timing.

RI-JRN04 M-P17's {top:0,right:44,bottom:21,left:44} cutout is the case that matters and it is untested.

attack_G_the_black_screen.said_plainly: A desktop browser at a phone-sized viewport is not a phone. Nothing done on this machine can tell the owner why a real device shows black; every check here says the build is fine, which is exactly the situation the dispatch described.
what_index_html_gets_right: probes WebGL before anything else, so a device that will never draw is not told to keep waiting
wraps fetch to catch a 404, the commonest silent black screen on a static host
distinguishes 'booted but painted nothing' from 'never booted' — and the comment records that hiding on the harness object's existence was wrong and cost the owner a second black screen
catches webglcontextlost, which fires an event rather than throwing and would otherwise be invisible
two_suspicions_of_mine_that_were_wrong_a: the canvas is STATIC in the HTML (<canvas id='view'>, line 49), so the context-lost listener does bind
renderer.js:48 sets preserveDrawingBuffer: true, so painted()'s readPixels outside a rAF callback is valid rather than reading a cleared buffer
missing_in_priority_order: navigator.userAgent — NOT COLLECTED ANYWHERE IN THE FILE (grep -c userAgent -> 0). For a phone-only failure this is the single most useful line on the screen; without it nobody can tell which device the report came from.

shader compile/link failure — the most likely cause of a black screen that gets as far as 'the world loaded, but nothing is being drawn'. Three.js reports a failed shader through console.error, NOT a thrown exception, so window.onerror never fires and the notice reports the symptom with none of the cause. Patching console.error to capture the first line containing 'THREE.WebGLProgram' would turn the owner's screenshot into a diagnosis.
gl.getShaderPrecisionFormat(gl.FRAGMENT_SHADER, gl.HIGH_FLOAT).precision — a GPU offering only mediump in fragment shaders is a classic mobile-only black screen, and it costs one line
MAX_VARYING_VECTORS, MAX_FRAGMENT_UNIFORM_VECTORS, MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS — the limits that actually make a mobile shader fail to link; MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE rarely does
navigator.deviceMemory / hardwareConcurrency, for the memory-pressure hypothesis
attack_G_the_black_screen.hypothesis_offered_as_hypothesis: renderer.js:50 sets setPixelRatio(1) and sizes from canvas.width, which is 1920x1080 in the markup. With preserveDrawingBuffer: true the browser must keep a SECOND full 1920x1080 buffer — roughly 16 MB of GPU memory that exists only so __HARNESS.screenshot() can read pixels back. On iOS Safari, the strictest WebGL memory environment in common use, an oversized preserved drawing buffer is a well-known way to be handed a lost context on a device that runs everything else fine. CHEAP AND REVERSIBLE EXPERIMENT FOR ROUND 2: set preserveDrawingBuffer: false unless ?harness=1 is present, and size the drawing buffer from the viewport rather than the markup. It costs the harness nothing in play mode. I could not test it — I do not have a phone — and I would rather name a testable hypothesis than score the diagnostics and move on.

my_own_instrument_errors_reported.what: The first run of --leg fight published EIGHT red checks: no swing, no roll, no guard, no damage. Every one was a broken probe. engine.js:3372 hands the latched input to the TITLE SURFACE and returns before stepCombat is ever reached, so the fixture was tapping an attack button at a menu.
my_own_instrument_errors_reported.what_caught_it: the DESKTOP control arm — a real mouse press on Mouse0, which IS 'light' on the keyboard profile, produced exactly the same nothing. A teardown that turns every arm red including the one that is supposed to work is not a finding, it is a broken instrument (RULES 4).
my_own_instrument_errors_reported.cost_if_shipped: this verdict would have said a phone cannot fight, on a build where it can

my_own_instrument_errors_reported.what: My C-BLOCK red in --leg fight was also false — measured with the body still in recovery from six swings and a roll. Measured cleanly it passes 20/25.
My first roll check called `backstep` a failure. A dodge with no direction IS a backstep in both source games; the check was wrong, not the build.

The second half of my own tools/touch/critic-differential.mjs is a BROKEN PROBE and its verdict line 'ACCEPTANCE 6 FAILS' is wrong and must be ignored. It dismisses the title with `Space`, which IS the roll binding, so the dismissal press and the roll press are the same key; and its sample windows overlap the previous action's recovery. It reported ['r1.1'] and ['guardbreak'] for a 'Space roll' — both ATTACK moves, neither a roll — which is the signature of reading the wrong window rather than of a build that cannot roll.
my_own_instrument_errors_reported.kept_not_deleted: The defect is documented at the top of the file rather than deleted, because a critic that hides its own broken arm is doing the thing this project keeps catching other people doing.
my_own_instrument_errors_reported.where_the_real_evidence_is: critic-roll-matrix.mjs arm D (pure desktop, KeyW + Space -> move `roll`, states ROLL_STARTUP/ROLL_IFRAME/ROLL_RECOVER, stamina 103.3 -> 82.8) and critic-block-roll.mjs (KeyF held -> guardRaised 9/15, state BLOCK_HOLD). The GEOMETRY half of critic-differential.mjs is sound and is what the verdict cites.

consumption.method: Each model perturbed IN THE DATA on a copy of the tree; the observable is a finger on real glass (RI-JRN04 CONSUMPTION §2 names 'an input that is accepted or refused' admissible and rules a harness return value out). Two well-separated values plus a null control, everything else held fixed.

M1 profiles.json touch.buttons[] geometr.perturbation: move the 'light' row 200 px left and 60 px up
M1 profiles.json touch.buttons[] geometr.observable: does a finger at ONE FIXED screen point swing?
M1 profiles.json touch.buttons[] geometr.perturbed: same point -> NOTHING; new centre (537,182) -> swings
M1 profiles.json touch.buttons[] geometr.why_this_is_the_strongest_form: the same input accepted, then refused, then accepted somewhere else, driven purely by a number in a data file, with the finger held at a fixed screen point across arms so the data moving under a stationary thumb is the only variable

M2 touch.stick.max_radius_css_px.observable: metres walked for one fixed 45 px finger displacement

M3 hold_gate.frames.observable: the running game's own gate value

M4 touch.camera.deg_per_css_px_yaw.observable: camera yaw after a fixed 100 px drag
M4 touch.camera.deg_per_css_px_yaw.note: moved by exactly the factor the data moved by, which is the check that the coupling is the real one and not a coincidence

null_control.result: light@(737,242), walked 0.193 m, camera -28 deg, swung true — identical to baseline on every observable
